## The part of code that seems to be the problem

  * `yt-dlp/yt_dlp/extractor/niconico.py`


    
    
    class NiconicoBaseIE(InfoExtractor):
        _API_BASE = 'https://nvapi.nicovideo.jp'
        _BASE_URL = 'https://www.nicovideo.jp'
        _GEO_BYPASS = False
        _GEO_COUNTRIES = ['JP']
        _HEADERS = {
            'X-Frontend-ID': '6',
            'X-Frontend-Version': '0',
        }
        _LOGIN_BASE = 'https://account.nicovideo.jp'
        _NETRC_MACHINE = 'niconico'
    
        @property
        def is_logged_in(self):
            return bool(self._get_cookies('https://www.nicovideo.jp').get('user_session'))
    
        def _raise_login_error(self, message, expected=True):
            raise ExtractorError(f'Unable to login: {message}', expected=expected)
    
        def _perform_login(self, username, password):
            if self.is_logged_in:
                return
    
            self._request_webpage(
                f'{self._LOGIN_BASE}/login', None, 'Requesting session cookies')
            webpage = self._download_webpage(
                f'{self._LOGIN_BASE}/login/redirector', None,
                'Logging in', 'Unable to log in', headers={
                    'Content-Type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded',
                    'Referer': f'{self._LOGIN_BASE}/login',
                }, data=urlencode_postdata({
                    'mail_tel': username,
                    'password': password,
                }))
    
            if self.is_logged_in:
                return
            elif err_msg := traverse_obj(webpage, (
                {find_element(cls='notice error')}, {find_element(cls='notice__text')}, {clean_html},
            )):
                self._raise_login_error(err_msg or 'Invalid username or password')
            elif 'oneTimePw' in webpage:
                post_url = self._search_regex(
                    r'<form[^>]+action=(["\'])(?P<url>.+?)\1', webpage, 'post url', group='url')
                mfa, urlh = self._download_webpage_handle(
                    urljoin(self._LOGIN_BASE, post_url), None,
                    'Performing MFA', 'Unable to complete MFA', headers={
                        'Content-Type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded',
                    }, data=urlencode_postdata({
                        'otp': self._get_tfa_info('6 digit number shown on app'),
                    }))
                if self.is_logged_in:
                    return
                elif 'error-code' in parse_qs(urlh.url):
                    err_msg = traverse_obj(mfa, ({find_element(cls='pageMainMsg')}, {clean_html}))
                    self._raise_login_error(err_msg or 'MFA session expired')
                elif 'formError' in mfa:
                    err_msg = traverse_obj(mfa, (
                        {find_element(cls='formError')}, {find_element(tag='div')}, {clean_html}))
                    self._raise_login_error(err_msg or 'MFA challenge failed')
    
            self._raise_login_error('Unexpected login error', expected=False)

Video download will not be faulty even logged in to the niconido with username and password.

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Multilingual videos on arte.tv produce inconsistent format sorting for audio formats when using different UI languages URLs to do the download. The most preferred video seems to always be the "correct" one, but beyond that the order does not make much sense.

Note that the format note showing the same language for every format has a separate issues already :[#11501](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11501).

Instead we likely should just take the order as it is present in the manifest as preference. This is the same order that is presented to the user in the UI. If the website is relying on it, so can we.
    
    
    LANGUAGE="de",NAME="Deutsch"
    LANGUAGE="en",NAME="Englisch (Original)"
    LANGUAGE="fr",NAME="Französisch"
    LANGUAGE="es",NAME="Spanisch"
    LANGUAGE="de",NAME="Deutsch (Klare Sprache)"
    LANGUAGE="de",NAME="Deutsch (Audiodeskription)"
    LANGUAGE="fr",NAME="Französisch (Klare Sprache)"
    LANGUAGE="fr",NAME="Französisch (Audiodeskription)"
    

[](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/26507958/650719189-88f09f89-84fe-465a-b6fb-0134e02936c2.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..-_StRBSG9ke3_mnN4Ts0wxNL2efY3B0CuBEcXd4bF_0)

Manifest format order for other UI languages:
    
    
    LANGUAGE="fr",NAME="français"
    LANGUAGE="en",NAME="anglais (VO)"
    LANGUAGE="de",NAME="allemand"
    LANGUAGE="es",NAME="espagnol"
    LANGUAGE="fr",NAME="français (confort audio)"
    LANGUAGE="fr",NAME="français (audiodescription)"
    LANGUAGE="de",NAME="allemand (confort audio)"
    LANGUAGE="de",NAME="allemand (audiodescription)"
    
    
    
    LANGUAGE="es",NAME="español"
    LANGUAGE="en",NAME="inglés (originale)"
    LANGUAGE="fr",NAME="francés"
    LANGUAGE="de",NAME="alemán"
    LANGUAGE="fr",NAME="francés (voces más claras)"
    LANGUAGE="fr",NAME="francés (audiodescripción)"
    LANGUAGE="de",NAME="alemán (voces más claras)"
    LANGUAGE="de",NAME="alemán (audiodescripción)"
    

Some information also in [#17614 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17614#issuecomment-5562637032)

### Region

Australia

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

ABC iView, Australia playlist URLs are normally recognised by yt-dlp as such and all episodes in a show are downloaded. I noticed yesterday that there is now an error: "Unable to extract initial state".

I have encountered the error with a variety of shows uploaded recently and others uploaded 2 years ago suggesting iView have changed the backend of all pages. Have also tested individual seasons as well as groups of seasons.

I have attached verbose logs of the error and of a successful download from 2025.

  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

_No response_

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

If using `--lazy-playlist` and using `-O playlist:%(playlist_count)s` and using a `ytsearch` pseudo-URL, `NA` is returned, even though the playlist count should be available by the time of that `WHEN`.  
~~This may be a core issue and not one specific to youtube but I'm not sure of that.~~ This does NOT happen with a regular playlist (`youtube:tab`) (`playlist_count` is returned even if `--lazy-playlist` is specified), so this is an extractor-specific issue.

Edit: While it doesn't happen with a regular playlist (`youtube.com/playlist?list=`), it does also happen with channels:

\--lazy-playlist + @channel/videos

Issue body actions

Some known common issues. Make sure to always check this before opening issues. **Duplicates of these will be strictly treated as spam!**

**Useful issue tracker filters:**

[[Core Issues]](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Aenhancement%2Cbug%2Ccore%3Adownloader%2Ccore%3Apost-processor%2Ccore%3Aextractor%2Ccore%3Anetworking%2Ccore%3Acookies) [[Site Issues]](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Asite-request%2Csite-enhancement%2Csite-bug) [[YouTube issues]](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Asite%3Ayoutube) [[Good issues for new devs]](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3A%22gateway-issue%22)

## High priority issues

  * **[[Youtube] ERROR: Video unavailable. Playback on other websites has been disabled by the video owner (web_embedded player response playability status: UNPLAYABLE) #17497](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17497)**
  * **[[Youtube] ERROR: The page needs to be reloaded (tv_downgraded player response playability status: UNPLAYABLE) #17389](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17389)**
  * [[Youtube] Only format 18 (360p) is available for age-restricted videos #17542](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17542)



## Intractable issues

  * **[[YouTube] This content isn't available, try again later. #11426](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11426)**
    * You are exceeding the rate limit. Refer to [the wiki on how to avoid](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Extractors#this-content-isnt-available-try-again-later).
  * **[Passing Youtube cookies doesn't seem to work; cookies are being invalidated quickly #8227](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8227)**
    * [How to effectively export YouTube cookies](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Extractors#exporting-youtube-cookies)
  * **[[youtube] Sign in to confirm you’re not a bot #10128](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10128)**
    * Your IP has been blocked by YouTube while you are logged out. You can [pass logged-in cookies](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Extractors#exporting-youtube-cookies); however, doing so may get your account blocked. The safer solution is to use a different IP.
    * To prevent this, [try using a PO Token provider](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/PO-Token-Guide), though it will not help if your IP is already blocked.
  * **[[youtube] "Video unavailable" with cookies - YouTube blocking accounts from web #10085](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10085)**
    * Your account has been blocked by YouTube, or the video is not available in your region.
    * Avoid passing cookies, or add a [sleep delay](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#workarounds) to each download.
  * **[[Youtube] Immediate HTTP Error 403 on download #11868](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11868)**
    * Try using `--force-ipv4`, try using yt-dlp from a different IP address (e.g. disable your VPN), try using logged-in cookies if you were using yt-dlp logged-out, or try using yt-dlp without cookies if you were using logged-in cookies

  * [[Ixigua] ERROR: Failed to get SSR_HYDRATED_DATA #5374](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5374)
  * [Douyin always errors saying fresh cookies are needed, even when passing them #9667](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/9667)
  * **[[TikTok:live] Livestreams are mistaken as "not currently live" after JSON metadata request #11921](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11921)**
  * **[[tiktok:live] Unable to download JSON metadata: HTTP Error 400: Bad Request #16850](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16850)**
  * [[tiktok] API returns empty response #13134](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/13134)
  * [[TikTok] One format, varying results (region-related) #15690](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15690)
  * **[[TikTok] Unable to extract universal data for rehydration #17393](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17393)**
  * [Only audio downloads for TikTok videos that have a shopping cart #13928](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/13928)
  * **[[BiliBili] Unable to download webpage: HTTP Error 412: Precondition Failed #14830](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/14830)**
  * [[LinkedIn] Unable to extract video from LinkedIn group post #16531](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16531)



# External issues

  * **[[Youtube] HTTP Error 403 when using bgutil-ytdlp-pot-provider plugin #17368](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17368)**
  * [ffmpeg can't seek in Youtube's iOS m3u8 streams / `--download-sections` only downloads audio #9552](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/9552)
    * Use `-S proto:https` or `--extractor-args "youtube:player_client=default,-ios"`
  * [`--cookies-from-browser` "Permission denied" errors when Chrome/chromium-based browser is open in Windows #7271](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7271)
    * Try after closing chrome completely OR
    * Launch chrome from command line w/ `chrome.exe --disable-features=LockProfileCookieDatabase`
    * Alternatively, you can [install](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#installing-plugins) the [ChomeCookieUnlock yt-dlp plugin](https://github.com/seproDev/yt-dlp-ChromeCookieUnlock)
  * [`--cookies-from-browser`: WARNING: failed to decrypt with DPAPI / ERROR: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'decode' #10927](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10927)
  * [[youtube] Is downloading a livestream in 1440p or 2160p no longer available? #11262](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11262)
  * [[Youtube] 8k VR180 SBS videos no longer available #9903](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/9903)
    * Use `--extractor-arg "youtube:player_client=android_vr,default"`
  * [[Youtube] throttling and inconsistent speed in Russia #10443](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10443)
    * [Workarounds](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10443#issuecomment-2248940967)
  * [[Discord bot] Music stops in the middle #8854](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8854)
  * [[youtube] Endless "Incomplete data received" when downloading playlist #10394](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10394)
    * Don't use `--extractor-retries infinite`
  * [FFMPEG "Invalid data found when processing input" on live/post-live/dash videos (duplicate ftyp) #8641](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8641)
    * Regression in ffmpeg 6.1. Upgrade to ffmpeg 6.1.1 or to [master build](https://github.com/yt-dlp/FFmpeg-Builds/releases) revision `N-112916` or later
  * [[youtube] "Invalid data found when processing input" / ffmpeg errors on HDR VP9 in mp4 #7541](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7541)
    * ffmpeg bug. Upgrade to ffmpeg 7.0.1 or to the latest [master build](https://github.com/yt-dlp/FFmpeg-Builds/releases)
  * [`--mark-watched` fails with urlopen error #8149](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8149)
    * Disable pi-hole or whitelist `s.youtube.com`
  * [Chapter Embedding Results in Unnamed Chapters When Using Recent FFmpeg Builds #6859](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6859)
    * ffmpeg regression. Use <https://github.com/yt-dlp/FFmpeg-Builds> or upgrade to 6.1.1 or newer
  * [yt-dlp is detected as a virus #25](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/25)
    * It's a false positive. Complain to your vendor. There is nothing we can do
  * [Incomplete Data Recieved #1787](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1787)
    * Broken from Youtube's side. If downloading comments, use `-i` to ignore the error
  * [Wrong year in metadata in M4A, MP4, FLAC format #3087](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3087)
    * Workaround: `--parse-metadata "%(release_year,upload_date).4s:(?P<meta_date>.+)"`
  * [pyinstaller temp files are not cleaned up when using yt-dlp.exe with mpv #10294](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10294)
  * [Long Start-Up Time for `yt-dlp_macos` #10425](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10425)
  * [`--download-sections` / ffmpeg fails to seek in a 26+ hour long Twitch m3u8 #5372](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5372)
  * [Using proxy and `--download-sections`/ ffmpeg fails with HTTP Error 400/401/403 #12915](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/12915)



# FAQ

See <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ>

  * **[How to avoid Youtube's new "Super Resolution" AI-upscaled formats #15325](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15325)**
  * **[Getting deno to work in Termux. #15095 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15095#issuecomment-3544324838)**
    * Run a full Termux upgrade with `pkg update && pkg upgrade` before `pkg install deno`
  * **[[YouTube] Enhanced bitrate no longer available to download? #14133 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/14133#issuecomment-3217679575)**
  * [**Filename too long**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1136#issuecomment-932077195)
    * Use `-o "%(title).150B [%(id)s].%(ext)s"`
  * **[[YouTube]`--write-comments`: "Incomplete data received. Giving up after 3 retries" warnings #15435](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15435)**
  * **[twitter: No video could be found in this tweet #14742](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/14742)**
  * [[Question] odd ba* format selection? #979 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/979#issuecomment-919629354)
    * Generally do not use `ba*`
  * [Fix playlist_index's inconsistent behavior #302](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/302)
    * Check `playlist_autonumber` and `--compat-option playlist-index`
  * [yt-dlp python module not compiling with pyinstaller #3845](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3845)
    * Use `bundle/pyinstaller.py`
  * [Subtitle file is not deleted after being embedded #630 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/630#issuecomment-893659460)
    * Use `--compat-option no-keep-subs`
  * [`--download-sections`/`--sponsorblock-remove` does not cut at exact point #4216](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4216) / [YouTube Clip Downloads have unintented extra beginning part with no video #5080](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5080)
    * Use `--force-keyframes-at-cuts`
  * [Duplicating pull request from youtube-dl to yt-dlp #4202](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4202)
  * [How to check in browser if the video is DRM protected](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4062#issuecomment-1153474056)
  * [\--cookies-from-browser for a chrome/firefox like browser or non-default install location #2903](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/2903)
  * [What are yt-dlp's error codes? #4262 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4262#issuecomment-1173133105)
  * [Extractor option `language` for `crunchyrollbeta` #4640](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4640)
  * [Ability to strip Emoji from downloaded file  #4836](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4836) / [File names use "full-width" special characters: '？' vs '?' #5014](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5014)
  * [[Youtube] Extract exact timestamps #1803](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1803)
  * [[Feature Request] Crop to square thumbnail when embedding in MP3s #429 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/429#issuecomment-2282554440)
  * Download only videos with subtitles 
    * `--parse-metadata "%(subtitles.\:.0.ext|)s:^(?!\[\])(?P<has_subs>.)" -v --match-filter has_subs`
  * [How do I rename previously-downloaded files with nothing but the youtube video ID? #5692](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5692)
  * Remove specific fields from info-json - [[Suggestion] Redact `formats` in info json with an option #455 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/455#issuecomment-1367741786)
  * About subtitles in mp4 container - [Convert webvtt subtitles in mp4 into useable format #5833 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5833#issuecomment-1358246240)
  * [Find the API option for a CLI argument #5859 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5859#issuecomment-1363938900)
    * Use <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/devscripts/cli_to_api.py>
  * [[YouTube] `youtube:skip=translated_subs` doesn't work for some videos. #3875](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3875)
  * [Youtube bestvideo and vp9 preference. #1232 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1232#issuecomment-939635345)
  * [repo: git log broken by SSH signature #7322](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7322)
  * [download comments into separate comments.json file #2372 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/2372#issuecomment-1506413976)
  * [How to force a conversion to a specific video codec? #7607 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7607#issuecomment-1636960750)
  * [How to download youtube videos in mp4 format? #8880](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8880)
  * [How do I properly pass my Soundcloud oauth token to yt-dlp? #12249 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/12249#issuecomment-2628937389)
  * [[youtube] 256kbps music formats not being extracted #12455 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/12455#issuecomment-2677077342)
  * [[PYI-12704:ERROR] Failed to extract Cryptodome\Cipher_ARC4.pyd: decompression resulted in return code -1! #16522](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16522)
    * You probably don't have enough free disk space on the drive where your temp dir is located



**PS** : These are just the most common issues at the moment. Make sure to [search for duplicates](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) in general before opening issues. Looking at this is not an excuse to not search for other duplicates!

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Korea

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

If the SOOP subscription-only VOD is a multi-part VOD, an HTTP 403 error occurs when the HLS download starts for the first part, but the last part downloads normally.

Playback proceeds normally in a browser using the account used in the command line.

Possible Cause

  1. Part 1 authentication
  2. Part 1 m3u8 extraction
  3. Part 2 authentication
  4. Part 2 m3u8 extraction
  5. Using Part 2 authentication credentials when downloading Part 1 m3u8
  6. HTTP 403 error
  7. Using Part 2 authentication credentials when downloading Part 2 m3u8
  8. Download successful



### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

Pinned comment options

[bashonly](https://github.com/bashonly)on Aug 20, 2026

Workaround: If you're passing logged-in cookies to yt-dlp, try without cookies. If you're getting the error without cookies, then you'll need use a [PO token provider](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/PO-Token-Guide) and the `mweb` client or (if logged-in) `web_creator` client.

This is a side effect of [#17389](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17389). The fix for that issue will also fix this one.

  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar questions **including closed ones**. ### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

I can't be sure this message when I tried opening Youtube today is related to this software or not.... I've never seen it before anyway... and I don't use anything else that I know of that might trigger this. I think I might have downloaded one hour long (low res) video of about 660MB yesterday only. Nothing like previously when a rogue playlist downloaded 90GB of youtube music videos!

I don't know what the timestamp of 15:03 is about... I was not near Youtube at all at that time. Anyway nice of them to throw that shit at a paying Youtube Premium member!

  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

# Windows filename sanitizer silently replaces ASCII "/" with U+29F8 BIG SOLIDUS #17549

[](https://github.com/pcheek1991)

[pcheek1991](https://github.com/pcheek1991)

opened [on Aug 27, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17549#issue-5270378235)

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

On Windows 11, yt-dlp silently replaces the ASCII forward slash "/" (U+002F SOLIDUS) in metadata used by an output template with U+29F8 BIG SOLIDUS.

The source title is:

Process serving Firestone (and/or)(or/and) Bridgestone on behalf of USAA per Patrick Jenks

The filename generated by yt-dlp contains:

Process serving Firestone (and[U+29F8 BIG SOLIDUS]or)(or[U+29F8 BIG SOLIDUS]and) Bridgestone on behalf of USAA per Patrick Jenks

Environment:

Windows 11  
yt-dlp master@2026.08.26.234438  
commit [`94eba4c`](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/commit/94eba4c156af080e87caf10cf8ffbea03bd17407)  
win_exe  
locale cp1252  
filesystem encoding utf-8  
output encoding utf-8

The behavior reproduces both when printing the generated filename and during an actual successful HLS download.

This is not an extractor failure. The source metadata contains the normal ASCII "/" character. The substitution occurs when yt-dlp constructs a filesystem-safe filename.

The substitution is problematic because U+29F8 is visually similar to "/" but is a different Unicode character. In a downstream Windows PowerShell 5.1 workflow, the UTF-8 bytes for U+29F8 were interpreted using a legacy Windows encoding and appeared as the mojibake sequence "a-section-sign-cedilla" rather than the intended character.

I understand that "/" cannot be used literally inside a Windows filename. The issue is the silent substitution with a Unicode lookalike rather than an ASCII-safe replacement, and the lack of an obvious warning or documentation describing this transformation.

Expected behavior:

Either clearly document the filename sanitization transformation from U+002F to U+29F8, warn when the substitution occurs, or provide a clearly documented ASCII-safe filename sanitization behavior for Windows.

Actual behavior:

ASCII U+002F "/" in the source title is silently transformed into U+29F8 BIG SOLIDUS in the generated filename.

The transformation also occurs with --skip-download and --print filename, demonstrating that it occurs in filename generation rather than during HLS downloading, ffmpeg processing, or filesystem writing.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm asking a question and **not** reporting a bug or requesting a feature
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar questions **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

##### What I want to do

When download <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6-2DAj39clo> video,  
Put the “Uploader” information in “Artist” instead of “AlbumArtist”

###### And I realized while writing this. Is this a bug?

When download <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IidyyM3giZw> with -f 251 -x option,  
in other words, if put into opus container,  
the "comment" metadata disappeared and, it put the "webpage_url" information in "description" metadata.

Please teach me what option I should write.  
I'm reading the modify metadata section but I don't quite understand it.

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

# [Youtube] Request for update of --datebefore --dateafter behaviour when downloading videos chronologically via channels. #11084

New issue

Copy link

New issue

Copy link

Open

Open

[[Youtube] Request for update of --datebefore --dateafter behaviour when downloading videos chronologically via channels.](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11084#top)#11084

Copy link

Labels

[questionQuestion](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22question%22)Question[site:youtube](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22site%3Ayoutube%22)

## Description

[](https://github.com/pxssy)

[pxssy](https://github.com/pxssy)

opened [on Sep 25, 2024](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11084#issue-2547768578)

Issue body actions

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a site-specific feature
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Singapore

### Example URLs

<https://www.youtube.com/@NileRed>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

When a youtube channel input like <https://www.youtube.com/@NileRed> is given to yt-dlp, it parses ALL /video and /shorts, then downloads them sequentially by chronological order, latest upload first, as its what is given by the API. Its not possible to sort in any other way.

In this case, If an option like --dateafter or --datebefore is used, many unnecessary requests are sent to youtube for videos that clearly will not match a filter.

Example

yt-dlp <https://www.youtube.com/@NileRed> \--dateafter 21001231 will match 0 videos, since the earliest video is in 2024. However it will check through EVERY video, even the ones before 2024, which is unnecessary and slow.

Similarly, yt-dlp <https://www.youtube.com/@NileRed> \--datebefore 00010101 will also match 0 videos, but it will check every video until the very first one.

Until youtube changes this, I believe this additional checks are not necessary at all.

Therefore I suggest 2 changes.

  1. \--datebefore runs the downloading backwards, starting from the oldest video in the channel.



EDIT: an existing workaround is -I "::-1"

  2. a switch like --date-skip 5, that skips process after it has checked 5 videos and they do not match the date requirements.



Expected behaviour should then be

yt-dlp <https://www.youtube.com/@NileRed> \--dateafter 20240101 --date-skip 3

Downloads videos after 20240101  
skip  
skip  
skip  
Download shorts after 20240101  
skip  
skip  
skip

exit

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

# Provide a Flatpak/Submit to Flathub #9808

New issue

Copy link

New issue

Copy link

Open

Open

[Provide a Flatpak/Submit to Flathub](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/9808#top)#9808

Copy link

Labels

[docs/meta/cleanuprelated to docs, code cleanup, templates, devscripts etc](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22docs%2Fmeta%2Fcleanup%22)related to docs, code cleanup, templates, devscripts etc[questionQuestion](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22question%22)Question

## Description

[](https://github.com/Throun)

[Throun](https://github.com/Throun)

opened [on Apr 28, 2024](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/9808#issue-2267274110)

Issue body actions

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

First off, thank you for this great project!

Atomic systems like Fedora Silverblue are commonly designed around using flatpaks as the primary, if not only, way of installing software, leaving users unable to use yt-dlp. There are some graphical programs available on Flathub that use yt-dlp, but they are limited in how much you can do compared to the command line. I believe the project should either build a flatpak or make a submission request to Flathub to allow affected users the ability to use this software.  
Flatpak also helps provide a standardized environment for users; what works on one system should work exactly the same on another. This might help weed out issues that are from distros/users rather than the project.

I have written a preliminary manifest that someone can use as a start if there is interest:  
[downloaders.yaml.txt](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/files/15140259/downloaders.yaml.txt)  
[org.yt_dlp.yt_dlp.yaml.txt](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/files/15140260/org.yt_dlp.yt_dlp.yaml.txt)  
[python3-modules.yaml.txt](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/files/15140261/python3-modules.yaml.txt)  
I am willing to answer any questions about this to the best of my ability.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

# Extractors: Availability of DOM query functions #10621

New issue

Copy link

New issue

Copy link

Open

Open

[Extractors: Availability of DOM query functions](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10621#top)#10621

Copy link

Labels

[questionQuestion](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22question%22)Question

## Description

[](https://github.com/Lalufu)

[Lalufu](https://github.com/Lalufu)

opened [on Aug 1, 2024](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10621#issue-2442230799)

Issue body actions

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm asking a question and **not** reporting a bug or requesting a feature
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar questions **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)



### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

I am looking into writing a new extractor, and I'm wondering if I'm missing some obvious utility functions for extracting information from a HTML page. I had, maybe naively, expected there to be functions similar to `document.querySelector()` and `document.querySelectorAll()` from JS, which take a more or less abstract path through the document and return matching elements, maybe backed by `BeautifulSoup` or other libraries. I have found the `get_element_*` functions from `utils`, which don't seem to quite do the same thing (I can't seem to look for tags of a certain type?), and looking at other extractors, using regular expressions seems to be pretty popular for some reason instead. There's also some xpath support, but from a quick look nothing seems to utilize this for dealing with HTML.  
Do functions like this exist, and I haven't found them, or is this a discouraged approach for some reason?

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)



### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

Ok so first, `--write-subs --use-postprocessor "subs_converter" --print "after_move:%(requested_subtitles.:.filepath)s"` works fine.  
But let's skip download cuz we are just for subs. `--write-subs --use-postprocessor "subs_converter" --print "after_move:%(requested_subtitles.:.filepath)s" --skip-download`.  
No print no postprocess.  
So I tried before_dl. `--write-subs --use-postprocessor "subs_converter:when=before_dl" --print "before_dl:%(requested_subtitles.:.filepath)s" --skip-download`. Sub is converted but the print happened before the postprocess so the output is wrong.  
But if I move the print to post_process it won't print `--write-subs --use-postprocessor "subs_converter:when=before_dl" --print "post_process:%(requested_subtitles.:.filepath)s" --skip-download`  
Now... what should I do, to download subs only and call the postprocessor and print the converted filename?  
Is there a stage between before_dl and post_process so I can print the result after the postprocess?

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)

  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

# Having yt-dlp create a symlink for playlists with a certain path #13674

New issue

Copy link

New issue

Copy link

Open

Open

[Having yt-dlp create a symlink for playlists with a certain path](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/13674#top)#13674

Copy link

Labels

[questionQuestion](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22question%22)Question

## Description

[](https://github.com/Aces-and-Jacks)

[Aces-and-Jacks](https://github.com/Aces-and-Jacks)

opened [on Jul 9, 2025](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/13674#issue-3214340349)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm asking a question and **not** reporting a bug or requesting a feature
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar questions **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

As far as I can see, no one has posted a question like this. I know you can use the `--exec` command for symlinks. But I'm not really code savy to figure this out. This probably isn't possible but I figured it wouldn't hurt to ask.

I currently have the videos I download symlinked as `--exec 'cd "/Users/$USER/Downloads/sym-folder" && ln -s --'`. Which worked well before. All my videoes get downloaded to their own folders as `/Users/$USER/YT-Downloads/%(uploader)s-[%(uploader_id)s]/%(uploader)s-%(upload_date>%Y-%m-%d)s_%(title)s-[%(id)s]/%(uploader)s-%(upload_date)s_%(title)s-[%(id)s].%(ext)s'` and the resulting files get symlinked to the other directory.

The thing is when I download a playlist, a folder that shows the playlist uploader gets created along with the other uploads for each video `%(uploader)s-[%(uploader_id)s]`. Which I'm fine with (I also see in the info file the playlist name and count it was with), but for the symlinked videos they just show without any filepath order. Which would make sense based on the file path. I tried using one of the fields in the OUTPUT TEMPLATE options but that didn't work properly. I figured it probably wouldn't tho.

I had asked for help for just symlinking in the past in [#11080](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11080) and based on what `bashonly` provided I tried to figure it out. He mentioned there was a field for `filepath` but I guess I had asked too many questions since he didn't answer, and I had already gotten my main question at the time answered. For symlinking he meantioned

> `ln -s -- %(filepath,_filename|)q`

but then said

> IMPORTANT: you should only ever use `%()q` in `--exec` arguments, and never `%()s`

So to sum it all up, I was wondering about a command that creates symlinks in a filepath that includes the playlist uploader. Like some sort of field string or something. I hope I didn't make this too confusing.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

## Description

[](https://github.com/dajotim937)

[dajotim937](https://github.com/dajotim937)

opened [on Jun 3, 2025](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/13381#issue-3113644843)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

So, here is related issue: [#6501](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6501)

But I'm asking not about overwriting original video file, but about final (opus in case of youtube) file that being overwritten.

Example:  
`yt-dlp.exe -f bestaudio --extract-audio --audio-quality 0 --parse-metadata "%(uploader)s:%(meta_channelName)s" --embed-metadata -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s" https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OcrsSaWZ4CY`  
This command download video and extract audio into 'Deja Reve.opus' file.  
Then:  
`yt-dlp.exe -f bestaudio --extract-audio --audio-quality 0 --parse-metadata "%(uploader)s:%(meta_channelName)s" --embed-metadata --no-overwrites "%(title)s.%(ext)s" -w https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L8M71Xu1rVc`  
And no warnings, no errors, just overwrite of final file.

Well, it's kinda hard to tell from first glance. Same track with same name and maybe yt-dlp just overwrite metadata.  
`yt-dlp.exe -f bestaudio --extract-audio --audio-quality 0 --parse-metadata "%(uploader)s:%(meta_channelName)s" --embed-metadata -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s" https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zIAku-Qwfl0`  
`yt-dlp.exe -f bestaudio --extract-audio --audio-quality 0 --parse-metadata "%(uploader)s:%(meta_channelName)s" --embed-metadata -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s" --no-overwrites https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cBQpZsnLyMw`

Yeah, nope. End up with second track that overwrite first one. So. Is it a bug? Or intended behaviour? How to prevent such behaviour if so (except puting something like %(id)s into filename)?

  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I need to get `engagementPanels` to get artist, track, album etc. info which `%(track)s`, `%(artist)s` templates don't return unfortunately to add it to downloaded video name. `player_responses` contains it in saint of saints `_real_extract()` method of YouTube extractor but final dictionary don't contains it, so it would be nice to get an optional `player_responses` `YoutubeDL` class parameter to append this in current `extract_info()` dictionary (and probably `--player-responses` CLI argument). I know that `engagementPanels` parsed to get comments and likes info but not video music info so I can get it manually.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Region

world wide

### Example URLs

<https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCFNS9Ajnby6Nr7WSz-qDa5g/posts>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Excluding videos that cannot be downloaded does not work for the Posts tab. Please:

  * Create a new option for this, or

  * Extend the --compat-options no-youtube-unavailable-videos option




These videos are usually private or country-restricted

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

India

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

[generic] squeezing-the-fresh-stuff: Downloading webpage  
ERROR: [generic] Got HTTP Error 403 caused by Cloudflare anti-bot challenge; try again with --extractor-args "generic:impersonate"  
[yt-dlp wrapper] Cloudflare detected - retrying with browser cookies + impersonation...

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

## Description

[](https://github.com/zozo1237)

[zozo1237](https://github.com/zozo1237)

opened [on Sep 19, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17701#issue-5507882736)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Today I realized that deno was out of date.  
Though I try to keep an eye on release notes I missed the [notice provided](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/releases/tag/2026.06.09). That really bites - I've archived thousands of videos since then that might be (are likely?) of lesser quality. Since a JS runtime is so important these days and this type of issue seems like it could've affected others I figured I'd raise an issue here.

[A warning if a JS runtime is out of date](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16969) or misconfigured would certainly help. Honestly though, if there is no valid JS runtime I'd rather yt-dlp just refuse to download anything from YouTube wholesale.

I propose a command line flag that prevents yt-dlp extractors that support JS runtimes from running if there is no valid JS runtime. Something like `--ensure-js-runtimes`

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output

### Example URLs

<https://youtube.com/allpossible/videos> or all other tabs

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

When you want to download a playlist, all videos (without filters, etc.) are downloaded.

Once a video has been downloaded, requests for the next video in the playlist start immediately.

I’d also like to have a 5–20-second delay between them.

Example:

youtu.be/video1  
sleep 5–20 sec  
youtu.be/video2  
sleep 5–20 sec  
.....

Currently in use (Copied from my config file)

##### Number of seconds to sleep between requests during data extraction

\--sleep-requests 6.39

##### Number of seconds to sleep before each subtitle download

\--sleep-subtitles 6

##### Number of seconds to sleep before each download. This is the minimum time to sleep when used along with --max-sleep-interval

\--sleep-interval 6  
\--max-sleep-interval 20

##### Time to sleep between retries in seconds

\--retry-sleep http:6.39  
\--retry-sleep fragment:6.39  
\--retry-sleep file_access:6.39  
\--retry-sleep extractor:6.39

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Germany

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

In Browser I can select 2K and 4k quality but yt-dlp shows just formats up to 1080p.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

## Description

[](https://github.com/WlaBo75)

[WlaBo75](https://github.com/WlaBo75)

opened [on Nov 25, 2024](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11627#issue-2689923572)

Issue body actions

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Using --download-archive options saves info about the already downloaded video. If the archive.txt file was changed manually, for example manually added "site video_id" for not available videos, yt-dlp ignores it until next start and is trying to downloadt it again. Often the same video is available miltiple times in the playlist. Could you please let yt-dlp to check this file not only at start but also for every not downloaded video.  
Many thanks in advance

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Netherlands

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

After fully downloading an ongoing stream (started downloading while it was going -> ended when it ended) with subtitles included in the command, the subtitles did not make it into the final video.

The only subtitles that got included is at the start of the video and it is a small segment from god knows where in the stream which consists of multiple lines some of which are repeating,

**I'm unable to include the verbose output since stream went subscriber only after finishing and the command no longer works.**
    
    
    ./yt-dlp --version
    2025.12.08

Command:
    
    
    ./yt-dlp --live-from-start "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SH3VUnXaw1I" --write-sub --write-auto-sub --sub-lang "en.*" --cookies-from-browser "firefox:<HIDDEN>" -k

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

## Description

[](https://github.com/WillPittenger)

[WillPittenger](https://github.com/WillPittenger)

opened [on Aug 30, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17571#issue-5289972349)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm requesting a site-specific feature
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

US

### Example URLs

[https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLkJADc1qDrr_eXSEaPOgTYM5uPQKOnQIf&index=27](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLkJADc1qDrr_eXSEaPOgTYM5uPQKOnQIf&index=27)

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I was downloading a YouTube playlist where 26 videos are marked private and were hidden. I have `--wait-for-video` on as I commonly start downloads of live videos from the command line. But in this case, that was a problem. yt-dlp wanted to sit there on a video that wasn't live. The video might later be changed to be non-private, but that could be months away. It would help if there was a command line option that changed the behavior of `--wait-for-video` to never wait on private videos.

(I'm assuming this is mainly an issue for YouTube. Hence, I decided to treat it as a site feature request.)

It's possible `--ignore-private-videos` would actually be implemented as an extractor argument, however an alias would be handy.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

# [youtube] Multi-thread comments extraction #17591

[](https://github.com/BOplaid)

[BOplaid](https://github.com/BOplaid)

### Region

_No response_

### Example URLs

Any video with comments which have replies, e.g. me at the zoo: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jNQXAC9IVRw>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

The title may sound crazy but please bear with me.

Let's consider how an HTTP downloader multi-threads: It establishes multiple connections and requests the item being downloaded from the server from each connection. The main trick that it does is that it requests the file start from a different byte per each connection. In other words, it **splits the file into chunks and requests each chunk from the web server**.  
This, to my knowledge, is not possible with YouTube comments. The equivalent would be requesting a specific comments page number, and that is not possible due to the continuation token thing. YouTube serves such a token with the first page extracted, which, when used, results in the second page, which itself serves another token, and so on and so forth. However, I have an idea.

Look at this log:
    
    
    [youtube] Downloading comment section API JSON
    [youtube] Downloading ~10581006 comments
    [youtube] Sorting comments by newest
    [youtube] Downloading comment API JSON page 1 (0/~10581006)
    [youtube]     Downloading comment API JSON reply thread 1 (1/~10581006)
    [youtube]     Downloading comment API JSON reply thread 2 (8/~10581006)
    [youtube]     Downloading comment API JSON reply thread 3 (11/~10581006)
    [youtube]        Downloading comment replies API JSON page 1 (16/~10581006)
    [youtube]        Downloading comment replies API JSON page 2 (33/~10581006)
    [youtube]        Downloading comment replies API JSON page 3 (44/~10581006)

    [youtube]        Downloading comment replies API JSON page 14 (185/~10581006)
    [youtube]     Downloading comment API JSON reply thread 7 (194/~10581006)

    [youtube]        Downloading comment replies API JSON page 36 (421/~10581006)
    [youtube]        Downloading comment replies API JSON page 37 (431/~10581006)
    [youtube]        Downloading comment replies API JSON page 38 (442/~10581006)
    [youtube]        Downloading comment replies API JSON page 39 (454/~10581006)
    [youtube]        Downloading comment replies API JSON page 40 (464/~10581006)
    [youtube]        Downloading comment replies API JSON page 41 (474/~10581006)
    [youtube]        Downloading comment replies API JSON page 42 (484/~10581006)
    [youtube]        Downloading comment replies API JSON page 43 (495/~10581006)
    [youtube]        Downloading comment replies API JSON page 44 (505/~10581006)
    [youtube]        Downloading comment replies API JSON page 45 (516/~10581006)
    [youtube]        Downloading comment replies API JSON page 46 (527/~10581006)
    [youtube]        Downloading comment replies API JSON page 47 (537/~10581006)
    [youtube]        Downloading comment replies API JSON page 48 (547/~10581006)
    

As you can see, sometimes yt-dlp descends into a reply section. But what if another thread was spawned and the continuation token for the reply section was passed to it, while the original thread continued extracting the root comments?  
This new thread would begin extracting the reply section, going page-by-page in that reply section, while the original thread continues extracting the root comments (and spawning more threads).

In the above example (I mean the log), more than 9 threads would be spawned simultaneously and immediately after the first page is downloaded, and the original/main thread could continue with extracting the root comments, moving on to the second page and spawning more threads there if needed, and so on and so forth.

Here's a diagram that may or may not be helpful in your understanding of this:
    
    
    Main comments extraction thread extracts first page (Downloading comment API JSON page 1)
    |
    | Assuming three reply sections in this page, immediately spawn:
    |---> Reply section extraction thread ("Downloading comment API JSON reply thread X" and maybe "Downloading comment replies API JSON page X" (the latter cannot be multi-threaded to my knowledge, as the pages of a multi-page reply section behave just like the root comments; so they can't be multi-threaded))
    |
    |---> Same as above
    |
    |---> Same as above
    --------------------------------------------
    Main comments extraction thread extracts second page (Downloading comment API JSON page 2)
    |
    | Assuming five reply sections in this page, immediately spawn:
    |---> Reply section extraction thread ("Downloading comment API JSON reply thread X" and maybe "Downloading comment replies API JSON page X" (the latter cannot be multi-threaded to my knowledge, as the pages of a multi-page reply section behave just like the root comments; so they can't be multi-threaded))
    |
    |---> Same as above
    |
    |---> Same as above
    |
    |---> Same as above
    |
    |---> Same as above
    --------------------------------------------
    And so on and so forth.
    

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a site-specific feature
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))

  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

_No response_

### Example URLs

<https://soundcloud.com/miles-dll/late-night-disco>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

It would be useful for me to have the original filename of Soundcloud downloads which have downloads enabled, since the name of the file often differs from the `artist - title` displayed on Soundcloud. I'm not sure if there's an existing infodict field which would be appropriate to use, though.

This can be retrieved using a `HEAD` request to the url for the `download` format, which has the original filename in its `content-disposition`. This seems to already be done to get the file extension for the `download` format via the `urlhandle_detect_ext` function ([soundcloud.py#L289](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/yt_dlp/extractor/soundcloud.py#L289)), but it doesn't store the actual filename.

This may also be useful for any other sites which have similar downloading functionality which retains original filenames (Odysee i believe has this?)

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Downloading (with yt-dlp) and even watching streams from certain users is completely broken without using a feature called "Super low latency β".

There's this setting called Super low latency β, and Twitcasting describes it like this: "Prioritize low latency over sound quality stability". I tried to see what it did on a technical side, but all I saw were websocket connections, so I'm not too sure.

Without this setting, streams from certain users, like [this user](https://twitcasting.tv/chiyomaru5pb) (note: not actually sure what other users have this issue; so far it's just that one in particular), would have the audio suddenly stop or sudden buzzing noises to occur. When the setting is on, the audio continues as normal. Downloading from the stream, yt-dlp will suddenly fail for no reason, which is why in the second video I linked, I wrote up a python script that passes the command automatically; the downloaded videos inherit the audio problems. No, the issue doesn't come from the python script, it did this beforehand. I think the issue arose sometime around late October 2025 if I recall.

The logs of a stream downloaded without this option don't seem to have any obvious errors, besides "EOF while reading input".

  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

[](https://github.com/ganego)

DO NOT post duplicates



### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

Hello,  
the generic extractor [uses the html page title for the video name](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/yt_dlp/extractor/generic.py#L732C9-L732C15). Now I have a website that uses the generic extractor where this title is wrong (truncated). Why not use the title that is given in the flashvars instead and just in case this value does not exist, use the html page title?

Example KVS video (this is an example for KVS in the extractor source, my website is different): <https://youix.com/video/leningrad-zoj/>

Maybe replace it like this:
    
    
    title = flashvars.get('video_title')
    if not title:
        title = self._html_search_regex(r'<(?:h1|title)>(?:Video: )?(.+?)</(?:h1|title)>', webpage, 'title')
    

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

It seems that it doesn't understand the new format of broadcast URLs, where the id starts with /live-..._...  
on vk.ru - it just says "Unsupported URL"  
But vkvideo.ru complains about the same thing, but also redirects to badbrowser.php.

I haven't tried substituting any user agent into the commands.

## Description

[](https://github.com/kellnerd)

[kellnerd](https://github.com/kellnerd)

opened [on Aug 2, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17349#issue-5042564048)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm requesting a site-specific feature
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Germany

### Example URLs

<https://www.zdf.de/video/serien/a-good-girls-guide-to-murder-102/gutes-maedchen-boeses-blut-100>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I want to use the ZDF extractor to download a video with the best possible audio quality. Previously I've been using <https://mediathekviewweb.de/> where the HD option gives me a pre-merged MP4 with a 160kbps AAC audio stream. With yt-dlp the available audio streams seem to be 128kbps (AAC or OPUS) at most, regardless of the format being audio-only or pre-merged with video.

For the example video, MediathekView returns <https://nrodlzdf-a.akamaihd.net/dach/zdf/26/06/260624_2145_sendung_agg/1/260624_2145_sendung_agg_a1a2_6660k_p37v17.mp4>.  
URL rewriting seems to be their trick ([/src/main/java/mServer/crawler/sender/zdf/ZdfVideoUrlOptimizer.java#L78](https://github.com/mediathekview/MServer/blob/a84054474e1e830fae79445f066cfce0c22e25d8/src/main/java/mServer/crawler/sender/zdf/ZdfVideoUrlOptimizer.java#L78)), the 6628k format (128k audio + ~6500k video), which yt-dlp also offers, is replaced by 6660k (160k audio + ~6500k video).

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

# Supported sites

Below is a list of all extractors that are currently included with yt-dlp. If a site is not listed here, it might still be supported by yt-dlp's embed extraction or generic extractor. Not all sites listed here are guaranteed to work; websites are constantly changing and sometimes this breaks yt-dlp's support for them. The only reliable way to check if a site is supported is to try it.

  * **10play** : _10play_
  * **10play:season**
  * **17live**
  * **17live:clip**
  * **17live:vod**
  * **1News** : 1news.co.nz article videos
  * **1tv** : Первый канал
  * **1tv:live** : Первый канал (прямой эфир)
  * **20min** : (**Currently broken**)
  * **23video**
  * **247sports** : (**Currently broken**)
  * **24tv.ua**
  * **3qsdn** : 3Q SDN
  * **3sat**
  * **4tube**
  * **56.com**
  * **7plus**
  * **9c9media**
  * **9gag** : 9GAG
  * **9News**
  * **9now.com.au**
  * **abc.net.au**
  * **abc.net.au:iview**
  * **abc.net.au:​iview:showseries**
  * **abcnews**
  * **abcnews:video**
  * **abcotvs** : ABC Owned Television Stations
  * **abcotvs:clips**
  * **AbemaTV** : _abematv_
  * **AbemaTVTitle** : _abematv_
  * **AcademicEarth:Course**
  * **acast**
  * **acast:channel**
  * **AcFunBangumi**
  * **AcFunVideo**
  * **ADN** : _animationdigitalnetwork_ Animation Digital Network
  * **ADNSeason** : _animationdigitalnetwork_ Animation Digital Network
  * **AdobeConnect** : (**Currently broken**)
  * **adobetv**
  * **AdultSwim**
  * **aenetworks** : A+E Networks: A&E, Lifetime, History.com, FYI Network and History Vault
  * **aenetworks:collection**
  * **aenetworks:show**
  * **AeonCo**
  * **agalega:videos**
  * **AitubeKZVideo**
  * **Alibaba**
  * **AliExpressLive**
  * **AlJazeera**
  * **Allocine**
